findings.comment: No transformer-specific easements are shown on the site or plat plans. Define transformer easement areas around each of the five pads with appropriate width and clearly indicate on all relevant plans (Plat, Site Plan, Electrical Plan).
codeCitations: UCM § 1.10.3 (additional clearance and access easements may be required)
findings.observation: Sheet 2 (Plat) shows various easements recorded on the property (25' Drainage Easement, 5' Electric Easements, 7.5' Public Utility Easements, 10' Wastewater Easement). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows drainage, electrical, and public utility easements noted on the site plan. Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) shows transformer pad locations. However, NONE of the plan sheets call out or define transformer-specific easements around the five transformer pads with specified widths and accessibility requirements. Transformer equipment typically requires defined easement areas for AE personnel to access and maintain the equipment.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 and related provisions indicate that additional clearance and access easements may be required around transformer equipment for Austin Energy accessibility and maintenance. While general utility easements are shown on the plat, no transformer-specific easement areas are defined on the site plan with documented widths and boundaries. This is essential information for ensuring ongoing maintenance access and compliance with AE requirements. Missing transformer easement documentation is a deficiency.

findings.comment: Transformer pad easements are not shown or documented on the electrical plan. Establish and document transformer pad easements around all five pads with dimensions and widths specified by Austin Energy Design to provide the required access for equipment maintenance and accessibility. Show these easements clearly on the electrical plan with dimensions and callouts.
findings.observation: Review of Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) and the full site plan set reveals no explicit transformer easement boundaries, widths, or callouts shown around any of the five transformer pads. The plans do not identify specific easement areas reserved for Austin Energy accessibility and maintenance around the pads. While electrical easements are shown at certain property locations (e.g., 5' Electric Easement near Pads), no dedicated transformer pad easements with specified widths are documented.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 indicates that 'additional clearance and access easements may be required' for AE facilities. This grouping's Regulatory Overview states 'Transformer easements required around pads (width determined by AE Design for accessibility).' The absence of any easement boundaries, dimensions, or callouts specifically designating transformer pad easements on the plans indicates that this requirement has not been addressed. The applicant must demonstrate that the necessary easements have been reserved.

findings.comment: Transformer pad detail sheets meeting Austin Energy Design-approved specifications are not provided. Obtain AE Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets, specify pad dimensions (length, width, depth) for each of the five pads, document service type (single-phase or three-phase), and reference the AE Design approval on the electrical plan.
codeCitations: UCM § 1.18.0 (obtain transformer pad detail from AE Design)
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows five transformer pads depicted as small hatched rectangles with leader line callouts reading 'Electrical Transformer Pad.' However, the sheet provides NO specific dimensions for any of the pads (no length, width, or depth specifications). The sheet provides NO documentation of service type (whether single-phase or three-phase). No reference is made to Austin Energy Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets (typically found in AE's standard details or obtained through the Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) process). No specific pad dimensions or reference to AE Design approval document are provided in the preliminary design plan or any supplementary documents.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.5.2.6 and § 1.18.0 (Appendix) require that transformer pad installations be designed according to Austin Energy Design-approved specifications. These specifications include detailed pad dimensions that vary by service type (single-phase vs. three-phase) and equipment configuration. The absence of (1) specific pad dimensions, (2) service type specification, and (3) reference to or attachment of AE Design-approved detail sheets represents a significant deficiency. The 'preliminary' designation on this electrical plan suggests final details are pending, but the lack of any reference to AE Design specifications is a notable gap in the plan set.

findings.comment: Transformer pad dimensions are not specified on the electrical plan. Provide the pad dimensions (length × width) for each transformer and reference the corresponding AE Design-approved transformer pad detail sheet for the specified service type (single-phase or three-phase), demonstrating that the pad configuration matches AE Design specifications.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 depicts the five transformer pads as simple rectangular boxes without any dimension annotations (length × width), no pad specification callouts (e.g., '10'×10''), and no reference to AE Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets. The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan provides no electrical specifications document, transformer schedule, or AE Design approval letters. The plan notes reference Austin Energy Design reviews (per Electric Review section), but no ESPA documents, transformer pad detail sheets, or AE Design-approved specifications are included in the accessible documents.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.5.2.6 and the grouping description require that transformer pad dimensions match Austin Energy Design-approved specifications for the specified service type. The plans provide no dimensions whatsoever and no reference to AE Design detail sheets. The applicant cannot demonstrate compliance with this requirement without showing that the pad dimensions match AE Design specifications. The absence of any dimension callouts or reference to AE Design details constitutes a clear deficiency.

findings.comment: Each transformer must be labeled with its type: Pad-Mounted Transformer, Pole-Mounted Transformer, Vault, or Service Drop. Current labels 'Electrical Transformer Pad' lack explicit type specification.
findings.observation: Four transformers are shown on Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) with locations and routing identified. However, each transformer is labeled only as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' with no additional type designation. Vision analysis confirms: 'The transformers are solely labeled as "Electrical Transformer Pad". There is no information provided regarding size (e.g., kVA), specific type, or whether they are CT metered or building metered.'
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that drawings 'clearly delineate electrical infrastructure locations.' For Austin Energy personnel reviewing these plans, knowing whether transformers are pad-mounted, pole-mounted, vault-mounted, or service drops is critical for design coordination and construction. The generic label 'Transformer Pad' may imply pad-mounted, but explicit specification of type (using standardized designations like 'Pad-Mounted Transformer' or 'Pole-Mounted Transformer') is necessary to meet code documentation requirements.

findings.comment: Transformer type not specified. Each transformer pad must be labeled with its specific type: pad-mounted, pole-mounted, vault, or service drop. Add callout notes or legend entries identifying the type for each transformer on the electrical plan.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 electrical plan labels all transformer locations uniformly as "Electrical Transformer Pad" with no supplemental callouts, notes, or specifications indicating the type of transformer. The label alone provides no information to distinguish between pad-mounted, pole-mounted, vault, or service drop configurations. No notes on the electrical plan specify transformer type for the site.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that plans clearly delineate electrical infrastructure with sufficient detail for Austin Energy to verify that the proposed service configuration meets code requirements. Transformer type is fundamental information: pad-mounted transformers require specific clearances per UCM § 1.10.4; vault installations must demonstrate conformance with niche design requirements and Network Area restrictions (UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 3); pole-mounted units have different access and safety requirements. Omitting type designation prevents verification of compliance with clearance and placement standards.

findings.comment: Identify and show on plans a transformer-specific electrical easement with dimensions adequate to encompass the transformer pad location, all required clearance zones per UCM § 1.10.4 (ranging from 3-15 feet depending on side), and an access zone for Austin Energy operations and maintenance.
findings.observation: Sheet 9, 11, and 21 show various electrical easements (5' Electric & Tele. Easement, 5' P.U.E., etc.) labeled with recording information. However, these easements are shown as property-line-based boundaries and do not specifically delineate easement areas around the transformer pad locations. The grouping guidance states: 'Easement dimensions must be adequate to cover specific facility clearances and access requirements' and references UCM § 1.3.24 (Easements for Electric Distribution Facilities). No easement dimensions are verified against the specific clearance requirements for the transformer pads themselves (which require clearances ranging from 3-15 feet depending on side and use).
findings.reasoning: Austin Energy requires easements that are adequate in size to cover not only the physical location of electrical facilities but also the clearance zones and access areas required by code. The grouping notes state: 'There is no uniform "5-foot electrical easement" standard in Austin codes. Easement dimensions must be adequate to cover the physical location of facilities, required clearances per UCM § 1.10.4 (ranging from 3-15 feet depending on equipment side and configuration), and areas needed for construction, operation, maintenance, and access per UCM § 1.3.24.' Without showing transformer-specific easement boundaries with dimensions verified against code clearance requirements, compliance cannot be confirmed.

findings.comment: Electrical easement around transformer facilities not shown or not adequate. Show dedicated easement boundaries around each transformer pad sufficient to cover: (1) the physical equipment location, (2) all required clearances per UCM § 1.10.4 (10-15 feet depending on equipment side and access requirements), and (3) Austin Energy access and maintenance areas. Label easement with recording information or "to be dedicated" notation.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) shows 4 transformer pad locations but does not show any dedicated electrical easement boundaries or polygons around the transformer facilities. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows existing electrical easements on property boundaries (labeled as "5' Electric Easement") but does not show proposed easements around transformer equipment. The grouping overview notes that electrical easements must be adequate to cover: (1) the physical location of facilities, (2) required clearances per UCM § 1.10.4 (ranging from 3-15 feet depending on equipment side), and (3) areas needed for construction, operation, maintenance, and access. No such easement polygons are depicted in the site plan set.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.24 defines easements as property rights necessary to ensure safe construction, operation, maintenance, and access to electric facilities. UCM § 1.10.4 specifies varying clearance requirements: hot-stick use areas require 10-15 feet clearance; sides with controls require 5 feet clearance from fencing; sides without operators may be 3 feet from removable fencing. Each transformer requires an easement adequate to encompass all clearance zones and access areas. UCM § 1.16.0 requires that plans clearly show easement boundaries. The complete absence of transformer easement delineation prevents verification that property within the site is reserved for electrical facilities and that access for Austin Energy maintenance is protected.

findings.comment: Each transformer must be labeled with its size in kVA (e.g., '150 kVA Pad-Mounted Transformer' or '300 kVA Pad-Mounted Transformer').
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) labels the four transformers as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' with no size information. Vision analysis confirms: 'The transformers are solely labeled as "Electrical Transformer Pad". There is no information provided regarding size (e.g., kVA).' No kVA ratings, load specifications, or capacity information is provided for any transformer.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, transformer documentation must include sufficient detail for Austin Energy to coordinate service adequacy with the project's electrical load. Transformer size (kVA rating) is essential information for design review, equipment ordering, and installation planning. Without size specifications, Austin Energy cannot verify that the proposed transformers are adequate to serve the project and cannot identify any shortfalls or required upgrades.

findings.comment: Transformer size not specified. Label each transformer with its capacity in kVA (e.g., "50 kVA", "100 kVA") and include transformer specifications (phase, voltage, cooling method) on the electrical plan. Confirm with Austin Energy that the total proposed transformer capacity is adequate to serve all 39 units.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 labels all four transformer pads with the text "Electrical Transformer Pad" but provides no kVA size, capacity rating, phase configuration, or other specification. No notes on the sheet detail transformer sizes. The architectural and electrical load information that would determine required transformer capacity is not included in the site plan set.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires sufficient plan detail for Austin Energy to verify that proposed service meets project requirements. Transformer size is essential information: it determines clearance requirements, cable sizing, cooling needs, and whether additional transformers are needed. Omitting size makes it impossible to verify that the four transformers are adequate to serve 39 residential units, or that sizing complies with Austin Energy design standards.

findings.comment: Label each transformer with its metering method (e.g., 'CT Metered' or 'Building Metered') to indicate how service measurement will be configured.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformers but provides no labeling indicating metering method. Vision analysis confirms: 'The transformers are solely labeled as "Electrical Transformer Pad". There is no information provided regarding... whether they are CT metered or building metered.' No notation distinguishes between CT (current transformer) metered service, standard building metered service, or other metering configurations.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, transformer documentation must specify the metering method because this affects service design. CT metering is used for larger transformer capacities (typically above 75 kVA), while building-level metering may be used for smaller loads. The metering method impacts the location of meter installation, the service distribution enclosure configuration, and the overall electrical service design. Without this specification, coordination with Austin Energy and proper electrical design cannot be completed.

findings.comment: Transformer metering method not labeled. Specify for each transformer whether it is CT metered (with secondary meter locations) or building metered (with individual unit metering). If meters are grouped (served from one service connection), label the service distribution enclosure, wireway, and meter bank location with grouping notation and reference to UCM § 1.9.3.4.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 labels transformers only as "Electrical Transformer Pad" with no indication of metering method. The eight meter locations are labeled as "Electrical Meters" but no callout specifies whether each meter is CT metered or building metered, or whether meters are grouped per UCM § 1.9.3.4 requirements. Service distribution enclosure or wireway locations are not identified.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that plans clearly detail service infrastructure. Metering method (CT metered at the transformer vs. building metered) affects meter placement, conductor sizing, and point-of-service configuration. For multi-unit developments, UCM § 1.9.3.4 requires that when two or more meters are served from one service connection, meters and disconnects must be grouped in a common location (meter bank/SDE) with specified clearances and line-of-sight requirements. Omitting metering method prevents verification of compliance with grouping and accessibility standards.

findings.comment: Transformer easements not shown on electrical design plan. Provide easement exhibits showing transformer pad locations and surrounding easement areas (width and dimensions to be determined by Austin Energy Design standards) necessary for equipment accessibility and maintenance.
findings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows three transformer pads but provides no documentation of transformer easement areas around the pads. Plat sheet (Sheet 2) and easement exhibits would show recorded easements but transformer-specific easement areas are not indicated on any plan sheets. No easement diagram or table provided showing easement widths, dimensions, or locations around the transformer pads.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires transformer easements around pads with widths determined by Austin Energy Design for accessibility and maintenance. The electrical design plan must depict transformer easement areas (typically rectangular areas extending from the pad) to demonstrate adequate space for AE personnel to access, operate, and maintain equipment. The complete absence of any easement delineation around the transformer pads represents failure to document this requirement.

findings.comment: Transformer pad dimensions and Austin Energy Design detail references not provided on electrical design plan. For each of the three transformer pads, provide: (1) specific pad dimensions (length x width x depth); (2) confirmation of service type (single-phase or three-phase); (3) reference to applicable Austin Energy Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets; and (4) construction material and reinforcement specifications.
findings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows three transformer pads depicted only as dotted rectangular outlines with no dimensional specifications. No pad dimensions are provided (e.g., "5' x 5'", "6' x 8'"). No reference is made to Austin Energy Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets. No documentation of service type (single-phase or three-phase) appears on the electrical plan. Vision analysis confirms: pads are "depicted simply as a dotted rectangle" with no labeled dimensions or detail callouts.
findings.reasoning: The electrical plan shows transformer pad locations but provides no pad dimensions or reference to Austin Energy Design-approved specifications. Each transformer pad must be designed to AE Design standards and constructed to specific dimensions determined based on the service type and equipment to be installed. Without this documentation, the contractor would have no specifications for pad construction, and the pads may not meet AE Design requirements.

findings.comment: Transformer pad location and distance from existing overhead lines must be shown on the Electrical Design Plan. Identify all existing or proposed overhead electric lines (including those in Valley View Road right-of-way and on adjacent properties), and annotate distances from each transformer pad to the nearest overhead line. Ensure compliance with applicable clearance requirements.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pad locations with underground electric line routing but does not show: (1) overhead electric lines or existing overhead lines in the vicinity; (2) distances from transformer pads to any existing or proposed overhead lines; (3) any callout or note identifying relationships to existing overhead transmission or distribution lines that may cross the property. The site plan notes reference overhead electric lines (OHE) in the right-of-way along the southern and eastern boundaries, but no specific distance measurements or clearance information is provided relative to transformer locations.
findings.reasoning: Transformer pads must maintain adequate clearances from overhead lines during installation and operation. UCM § 1.16.0 requires showing transformer pad locations and distance from existing overhead lines to ensure safe installation and operation. Without these distances clearly marked, installation crews cannot verify clearances are adequate and safety cannot be assured. Existing overhead lines in/near the right-of-way must be explicitly referenced with distances to proposed transformers.

findings.comment: Electrical easement dimensions must be adequate to cover transformer facilities and required clearances. Analyze whether existing 5-foot electric easements shown on the plat are sufficient for the five transformer pads, or propose new/modified easements. Show all easement boundaries clearly on Site Plan (Sheet 9) and Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) with dimensions and recording information. Easement widths must accommodate the transformer pad physical location plus all clearance requirements (up to 15 feet depending on location and equipment orientation).
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows electrical easements labeled with recording information (Vol. numbers, Pg numbers, document references) such as '5' Electric & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 385 D.R.T.C.Tx.' and '5' Elec. Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14 Vol. 73, Pg. 76 P.R.T.C.Tx.' However, these labeled easements are plat-dedicated easements of record (existing easements), not proposed easements around the transformer facilities. The facts.md lists several existing electric easements (5' electric easements per plat documents) but no analysis is provided showing whether these existing easements are adequate to cover the 5 transformer pad locations, their required clearances (which can range from 3-15 feet per UCM § 1.10.4), and access requirements. No proposed electrical easement is shown around transformer facilities.
findings.reasoning: Electrical easements around transformer facilities must be shown or proposed with adequate dimensions to cover physical location, all required clearances per UCM § 1.10.4, and access requirements per UCM § 1.3.24. Existing plat-dedicated easements shown on Sheet 21 are 5 feet wide, but transformer clearance requirements can extend 10-15 feet depending on equipment orientation and building features. Unless a detailed analysis demonstrates existing easements are sufficient, proposed easement dedications or modifications must be shown.

findings.comment: Individual transformer labels are missing on the plans. Assign unique identifiers to each of the five transformer pads (e.g., 'XFMR-1', 'XFMR-2', 'XFMR-3', 'XFMR-4', 'XFMR-5') and show these labels clearly on Sheet 21 and on all other plan sheets where transformers appear. This will enable clear cross-referencing in specifications and coordination documents.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads marked with blue square symbols and labeled as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' at their locations (NW, W-central, SW, E-central, SE). While the transformers are labeled with the equipment type 'Electrical Transformer Pad,' they are not individually labeled with unique identifiers (e.g., 'XFMR-1', 'XFMR-2', etc.) that would allow specific reference in specifications, electrical calculations, or coordination with other disciplines. This generic labeling without individual identification creates ambiguity in referring to specific transformers.
findings.reasoning: Clear identification and labeling of each transformer is essential for permit review, coordination with other trades, and construction. Generic labels like 'Electrical Transformer Pad' do not distinguish between the five different transformers. Each transformer should be uniquely labeled so that specifications, clearance calculations, meter assignments, and building connections can be clearly correlated to specific equipment. This is standard engineering practice for electrical documentation.

findings.comment: Transformer size (kVA) must be specified for each of the five transformer pads on Sheet 21. Include a specification note, callout label, or table showing: (1) transformer kVA rating for each pad, (2) quantity (number of units at each location), (3) metering method, and (4) buildings served by each transformer.
findings.observation: The 5 transformer pads shown on Sheet 21 are labeled only as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' with no size specification. No callouts, notes, or specifications indicate the kVA capacity of any transformer. No table or legend provides transformer specifications. The vision analysis confirmed: 'Size/Capacity: Not specified' for all five transformers. Without size information, it cannot be verified that transformer capacity is adequate to serve the development's electrical demand.
findings.reasoning: Transformer size (kVA rating) is essential information for: (1) verifying adequate capacity to serve all buildings, (2) determining construction, operation, and maintenance needs, (3) establishing clearance requirements, and (4) coordinating with Austin Energy. UCM § 1.16.0 requires complete and detailed electrical facility information. Omitting transformer sizes is a significant deficiency.

findings.comment: Transformer pad dimensions must be shown on all plan sheets depicting transformers. Provide specific dimensions for each pad (length × width) on Sheet 21 and verify the same dimensions are shown on Site Plan (Sheet 9), Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), and Grading Plan (Sheet 11) where transformers are added. Typical pad-mounted transformer pads are often 24" × 36" or 30" × 48" - specify the exact size for this project.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pad locations marked with blue square symbols. No dimension callouts are provided on Sheet 21 for the pad dimensions themselves (length and width of the equipment pad). Vision analysis stated: 'Transformer pad dimensions not consistent across all plan sheets.' Since transformers are not shown on Sheets 9, 11, 31, or 12, pad dimensions cannot be verified on any sheet other than Sheet 21. On Sheet 21, no specific pad dimension measurements (e.g., 24" × 36", 30" × 48") are annotated.
findings.reasoning: Transformer pad dimensions (length and width) must be shown on all plan sheets where transformers appear to ensure consistency and allow verification of clearances and access. Sheet 21 shows transformer locations but no pad dimensions are annotated. Since transformers don't appear on other sheets, consistency across sheets cannot be evaluated. Standard pad-mounted transformer dimensions should be specified in the electrical specifications or on the plans.

findings.comment: Metering method must be labeled for each transformer on Sheet 21. Specify whether each transformer is: (1) CT metered (with meters located at individual buildings), or (2) building metered (with grouped meters at central location). This designation must correlate with meter locations shown on the plans and must confirm that meters remain within sight of transformers per UCM § 1.9.3.1.B.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads labeled as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' and 8 meters labeled as 'Electrical Meters' but does not provide metering method designations for any transformer. No notes or callouts indicate whether the transformers are: (1) CT metered (current transformer metered at transformer, with meters located remotely at buildings), or (2) building metered (meters located at each customer/building adjacent to transformer). The vision analysis confirmed: 'Metering Method: Not labeled' for all five transformers.
findings.reasoning: The metering method (CT metered vs. building metered) is critical information that determines: (1) where meters are located, (2) where service disconnects must be positioned, (3) clearance and access requirements, and (4) coordination between transformer location and meter location. UCM § 1.9.3.1.B requires meters to be within sight of the transformer. The metering method must be clearly specified on plans so that meter locations can be verified as compliant.

findings.comment: Specify whether transformers are oil-filled or dry-type on the Electrical Design Plan. If oil-filled: (1) Show transformer pad locations on Grading Plan (Sheet 11) with contour lines and spot elevations; (2) Add drainage arrows or notes confirming that ground grading slopes away from transformer pads and toward properties; (3) Verify that no oil spill pathway leads toward building foundations or sensitive areas.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 pad-mounted transformers but does not indicate whether they are oil-filled (which requires drainage considerations) or dry-type. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) does not show transformer pad locations, so there are no grading details or drainage arrows visible around any transformer pads. No contour lines, spot elevations, or drainage flow arrows are shown in the vicinity of transformer locations. If the transformers are oil-filled, UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 footnote 1 requires grading to direct liquid flow away from buildings.
findings.reasoning: Oil-filled transformers pose an environmental and safety risk if oil leaks. Grading must be designed to prevent spilled oil from flowing toward buildings. This requirement only applies to oil-filled transformers. Without: (1) specification of whether transformers are oil-filled or dry-type, and (2) grading details around oil-filled transformers (if applicable), compliance cannot be verified. The omission of transformer locations from the Grading Plan means this critical drainage requirement cannot be addressed.

findings.comment: Pad-mounted transformer coordination with Austin Energy Design lead not verified. Provide documentation or correspondence confirming that transformer locations and specifications have been coordinated with and approved by Austin Energy Design lead.
applicableAreas: transformer pad locations on site plan
findings.observation: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows transformer pads located on the site plan (transformer symbols and locations are indicated). However, no documentation or correspondence confirming that pad-mounted transformer installation has been coordinated with Austin Energy Design lead was located. The block content for Sheet 21 does not mention transformer coordination or approval.
findings.reasoning: When new buildings increase load and require pad-mounted transformers, the installation must be coordinated with Austin Energy Design lead per UCM § 1.16.0(6). This is required to ensure proper siting, sizing, and connection to AE infrastructure. The presence of transformers on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan suggests they are part of the project design, but coordination with AE Design (beyond the general completeness check) is not documented. Evidence of this specific coordination should be provided.

findings.comment: Indicate the horizontal and vertical distance between each transformer pad and the nearest existing overhead electric line to verify compliance with required clearance distances.
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows existing overhead electric lines (OHE) running along the southern and eastern property boundaries. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) also depicts existing overhead electric lines but does not indicate distances or clearance relationships between the transformer pads and these overhead lines. No dimension lines, callouts, or notes specify the horizontal or vertical distance between any transformer pad and the nearest existing overhead line.
findings.reasoning: Transformer pad placement must account for clearances to existing overhead electrical lines per National Electrical Safety Code (NESC) standards and Austin Energy design requirements. Showing the transformer pad location without indicating its distance from existing overhead lines creates ambiguity about whether clearances are adequate. This information is essential for Austin Energy design review and for construction coordination.

findings.comment: Provide transformer pad dimensions (length × width × height where applicable) on all plans where transformers are shown, ensuring dimensions are consistent across sheets and adequate for the specified transformer kVA rating.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows four transformers as rectangular symbols with no dimension callouts indicating pad width, length, or height. Sheet 9 shows one transformer symbol as a simple rectangle with no dimensions. Pad dimensions are not provided on either sheet, making it impossible to verify consistency or to confirm that the dimensions are adequate for the specified transformer size and clearance requirements.
findings.reasoning: Transformer pad dimensions must be consistent across all plan sheets and must be adequate for the specified transformer size. Different transformer kVA ratings require different pad sizes. Per UCM § 1.10.4, pad clearance requirements depend partly on equipment size. Without documented pad dimensions, reviewing agencies cannot verify design adequacy or construction completeness.

findings.comment: Clarification needed regarding the two transformer pads shown on Sheet 21 and whether they represent separate services with different voltages. Provide Austin Energy documentation (ESPA approval letter or Letter of Agreement) confirming whether the two transformers are part of a single point of service at one voltage, or whether exceptions to UCM § 1.16.0(5) have been approved for multiple service points or voltages. If the transformers are step-down stages of a single service, add labeling to Sheet 21 clarifying the service configuration and voltage(s).
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows two electrical transformer pads, which may indicate two service points, but the vision analysis and detailed examination do not reveal explicit documentation of service voltage or whether exceptions to the one-POS/one-voltage rule have been approved. The plan shows: 'Two proposed transformers shown, and both are explicitly designated as pad-mounted. One is located on the western side of the property...The second is located on the eastern side of the property.' The question is whether these two transformers serve different buildings with different voltages (which would violate the one-voltage rule) or whether they are both serving the same development at the same voltage (which would be acceptable step-down transformers). The blocks.md for Sheet 21 does not specify the voltage(s) for each transformer. No documentation from Austin Energy (ESPA approval, Letter of Agreement) was provided that would confirm whether exceptions to the one-POS/one-voltage rule have been approved.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(5) allows 'only one point of service and one service voltage' unless exceptions are 'approved by Austin Energy Design.' The presence of two transformers on the plan is not inherently a violation if they are both part of a single service point and serve the same voltage. However, without explicit documentation of the service voltage and Austin Energy approval for the transformer configuration, it cannot be verified whether the requirement is met. The grouping's regulatory overview states: 'Several infrastructure requirements cannot be determined from site plan review alone and require formal determination by Austin Energy during the Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) review process' and specifically lists 'Vaults and pedestals: Service type selection is made during AE Design coordination and documented in Letter of Agreement or ESPA approval.' Similarly, the one-POS/one-voltage requirement requires Austin Energy confirmation. This item cannot be marked pass without evidence of AE approval, nor can it be marked fail without evidence of AE non-compliance.
